ready2_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A block of mass \(m\) slides down a plane inclined at an angle \(\theta\) to the horizontal. If the coefficient of kinetic friction is \(\mu_k\), what is the block's acceleration down the incline?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A block of mass \(m\) slides down a plane inclined at an angle \(\theta\) to the horizontal. If the coefficient of kinetic friction is \(\mu_k\), what is the block's acceleration down the incline?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a pink block labeled m, placed on a green inclined plane; the angle of the inclined plane relative to the horizontal plane is labeled θ; the acceleration arrow a points downward along the inclined plane toward the right side; the kinetic friction coefficient μ_k is also marked in the figure. Then reason: Take downward along the inclined plane as the positive direction. The component of gravity mg along the direction of the inclined plane is mg sin θ, directed downward; the component perpendicular to the inclined plane is mg cos θ, so the normal force N = mg cos θ. Because the block is sliding downward along the inclined plane, the direction of the kinetic friction force is upward along the inclined plane, with magnitude f_k = μ_k N = μ_k mg cos θ. Write Newton's second law along the inclined plane: ma = mg sin θ - μ_k mg cos θ. Divide both sides by m, obtaining a = g sin θ - μ_k g cos θ.

raw_record.question_text: A block of mass \(m\) slides down a plane inclined at an angle \(\theta\) to the horizontal. If the coefficient of kinetic friction is \(\mu_k\), what is the block's acceleration down the incline?

method.method_draft: Use a force-balance along axes parallel and perpendicular to the incline. First read the diagram as a block labeled m on an inclined plane with angle θ to the horizontal, acceleration arrow a pointing down the slope, and kinetic friction indicated by μ_k. From the text, take that the block is sliding down the incline, so kinetic friction acts up the incline. Resolve gravity into components: mg sin θ down the plane and mg cos θ perpendicular into the plane. The normal force is N = mg cos θ, so kinetic friction has magnitude f_k = μ_k N = μ_k mg cos θ up the plane. Apply Newton's second law along the slope with down the incline positive: ma = mg sin θ - μ_k mg cos θ. Divide by m to get a = g sin θ - μ_k g cos θ.
